title: Differential photometry
intro: Compare AE UMa with nearby stars to see how its brightness changes over one night.
dataset: AE UMa practice · 24 FITS cutouts sampled across the original 158-exposure night · 30 seconds per exposure · luminance filter.
outcome: A light curve for AE UMa, the original image behind a measurement, and a choice of a saved plot or a numerical report.

steps.title: Enter Differential Photometry
steps.requires: Start Citizen Astronomy (CAst). Download either AE UMa ZIP above and extract it. Keep the **AE UMa practice** or **AE UMa full** folder handy.
actions: Under **Detect & Measure**, click **Differential Photometry**. If a different workspace is already open, choose **Mode → Choose Mode…** to return to this screen.
steps.check: The workspace opens with an **Open** button in its upper left. The curve on the launcher card is an illustration. Your own graph appears after processing.
steps.alt: Mode launcher with a numbered outline around the Differential Photometry card.

steps.title: Open the workflow window
steps.requires: You are in [Differential Photometry](#mode).
actions: Click the large **Open** button at the upper left of the workspace.
steps.check: A window named **Differential Photometry Workflow** opens. It contains **1. Folder**, **2. Pipeline**, and **3. Progress**.
steps.alt: Upper-left corner of the workspace with the Open button outlined.

steps.title: Browse for the image sequence
steps.requires: The [workflow window](#open) is open.
actions: In **1. Folder**, click **Folder**.
steps.check: A folder picker opens. Select one folder for the complete run, whether you use the practice set or the full sequence.
steps.alt: Folder section of the workflow showing the highlighted Folder button.

steps.title: Select the folder containing the FITS files
steps.requires: The [folder picker](#folder) is open.
actions: Select **AE UMa practice** for the 24-frame exercise, or **AE UMa full** for all 158 original frames. Choose the folder containing the FITS files.
Click **Choose**. On Windows, the native picker may label this button **Select Folder**.
steps.check: Check the count in **Ready**: 24 files for the practice set or 158 for the full night shown in the screenshot. If your count differs, select the extracted folder that directly contains the .fit files.
steps.alt: Directory field containing (small copy) AE UMa and the Choose button, marked 1 and 2.

steps.title: Start the measurement
steps.requires: The [folder scan](#choose-folder) has found 24 practice images or 158 full-sequence images.
actions: For this L-filter practice run, clear **Pull Periods** (1). Leave **Calculate Periods**, **Create Measurements Table**, **Calibration**, and **Star Alignment** unchecked. The folder contains science exposures with embedded sky coordinates and includes no calibration masters.
Keep **Brightest Variables** at **100%** so you can choose AE UMa yourself. Click **Generate** (2). Allow the catalog lookup to finish. A first run can need internet access.
steps.check: CAst opens **Select Sources To Process** when the list is ready. If CAst offers an existing result for this folder, opening it takes you directly to the results. The example used a saved field catalog and the images’ embedded coordinates. See the [example settings](#recipe) to reproduce this selection.
steps.alt: Workflow showing 158 loaded images, the cleared Pull Periods checkbox, 100% Brightest Variables, and Generate.

steps.title: Check how the example was measured
steps.requires: In the Differential Photometry workspace, choose **Settings → Open Settings** before starting a fresh run.
actions: Click the **Differential Photometry** tab (1). The example requested **5** for **Comparison Stars per Variable** (2). The number that can actually be used depends on the stars in the field.

To match the brightness selection, check **Use reference-star magnitude range**. Set **Min** to the lowest allowed value (−5) and **Max** (3) to **16**. The adaptive aperture scale was **1.60 × FWHM**, which sizes the measurement circle using the width of the star image.

Click **Save** if you changed settings, or **Cancel** if you were only looking. This example used the saved catalog for the field and the embedded sky coordinates in each FITS header, without repeating the Gaia cross-check.
steps.check: The resulting Scan Comps window offered four usable measured references. Catalog updates or different quality settings may change the available stars.
steps.alt: Differential Photometry settings showing five requested comparisons and a maximum reference-star magnitude of 16.

steps.title: Measure AE UMa only
steps.requires: The [source-selection window](#generate) is open.
actions: In the **Sources** search field (1), type **AE UMa**. Keep **Named variables** checked.
Click the **AE UMa** row (2). Its catalog is **vsx** and its type is **Variable**. CAst chooses comparison stars for the target automatically.
Click **Process Selected** (3). Wait for the workflow to finish measuring the images. If its progress window stays open after completion, click **Close**.
steps.check: The **Source Results** table contains AE UMa. A light curve is a sequence of brightness measurements, one for each usable exposure.
steps.alt: Source dialog filtered to AE UMa, with the search field, selected VSX row, and Process Selected button numbered.

links.label: What do the other process buttons do?

steps.title: Measure several objects instead
steps.requires: Open the [source-selection window](#generate) before processing.
actions: To measure the brightest few, set **Default selection** to **Absolute number of brightest stars** and enter a small count, such as **3** (1). Click **Process Default** (2).

To work by category instead, choose a category from **All types** (3) and narrow the list with **Sources** or **Designation Families**. Click **Process All Visible** (4) to measure every remaining row. A long list takes longer.
steps.check: After processing, **Source Results** lists the measured targets. Click a row to switch the light curve to that star.
steps.alt: Alternate selection routes showing the default count, Process Default, source-type filter, and Process All Visible.

steps.title: Select the measured star
steps.requires: The [reduction](#target) has finished, or you opened a cached AE UMa result.
actions: Click **Source Results** (1) below the plot.
Click **AE UMa** (2). The workspace connects the selected source to its light curve and image. Other rows can be comparison stars used to measure the target.
steps.check: Look for AE UMa in the plot title or legend. A blank graph in **Standard Magnitude** can mean that this filter has no usable standard magnitude. Choose the relative brightness axis in the next step.
steps.alt: Source Results tab and AE UMa row outlined below the light-curve panel.

links.label: Plot brightness relative to the comparisons

steps.title: Switch to differential magnitude
steps.requires: You have [selected AE UMa](#result).
actions: Open **Settings** (1) on the top menu bar, then move to **Light Curve** (2).
Open the **Y** list (3) and choose **Differential Magnitude**. Click outside the menu to return to the graph.
steps.check: The vertical axis now shows magnitude relative to the comparison stars. A smaller value means a brighter target relative to them. On the plotted axis, 500 × 0.001 means 0.500 magnitude. These L-filter frames can show changes in brightness without establishing a standard Johnson V magnitude.
steps.alt: Settings menu, Light Curve submenu and Y selector set to Differential Magnitude.

links.label: Compare the target with reference stars

steps.title: Compare the star with its references
steps.requires: AE UMa is selected. Use the [differential magnitude axis](#axis).
actions: Open the **Filter** list (1) beside **Open** and choose **L** for this sequence.
Turn on **Show references** (2) to display the comparison stars. If their traces move together with the target, inspect the images for clouds or tracking problems.
Turn on **Show check** (3) to include an independent check star when one was measured. For a clearer view of AE UMa alone, clear both switches.
steps.check: AE UMa brightens toward the end of the run while the comparison traces remain relatively flat. The practice download provides 24 epochs. The screenshot shows measurements from all 158 original exposures.
steps.alt: L filter, Show references and Show check marked above the real AE UMa light curve.

links.label: Try a different set of comparison stars
Keep the automatic set and inspect the images
Trace a point to its exposure
Save a picture of the curve

steps.title: Inspect a single frame or blink the sequence
steps.requires: A [measured target](#result) is selected and its image is visible on the right.
actions: Click **Center** (1) to bring the selected star into view. Use the mouse wheel over the star if you want a closer look. The small circle is its measurement aperture.
To inspect one exposure, open the **frame selector** (2) and choose a filename. Watch whether the aperture still encloses AE UMa.
To play the sequence, click **Blink** (3). Click **Blink** again to pause. Look for shifts, passing clouds, or a neighboring star entering an aperture.
steps.check: Changing the frame changes the filename and image. Use the measurement table to identify the exposure time and brightness for an individual observation.
steps.alt: AE UMa image pane with Center, frame selector and Blink numbered above the measured star field.

steps.title: Open the measurement table
steps.requires: An [AE UMa reduction](#result) is displayed.
actions: Click the **Measurements** tab beside **File Results**.
steps.check: On a fresh run with table creation turned off, a **Load Measurements Table** prompt appears. If rows are already visible, go straight to reading a row.
steps.alt: Results tab strip with Measurements outlined.

steps.title: Confirm that the rows should load
steps.requires: The [Measurements tab](#measurements) shows a **Load Measurements Table** prompt.
actions: Check the number of rows in the message. Each exposure may contribute several rows for different stars.
Click **Yes** to load those rows. Large tables can take a moment.
steps.check: The prompt closes and the **Measurements** table fills with filenames and values.
steps.alt: Actual table-load confirmation with Yes highlighted.

steps.title: Read a measurement and its source frame
steps.requires: The [Measurements table](#load-table) is populated.
actions: Click a row for **AE UMa**. Use the **File** column to identify the exposure; read across the selected row for the filter and measured values.
Scroll horizontally for additional columns. If a point looks unusual, compare its image with adjacent frames before deciding whether to use it.
steps.check: The image and details follow the selected row. For the first AE UMa row, **Diff Mag** is **0.4445** and **Error** is **0.0060** magnitude.
steps.alt: Populated measurement table with an AE UMa measurement row marked.

links.label: Choose a point directly on the graph

steps.title: Trace a plotted point to one exposure
steps.requires: The [measurement rows](#load-table) are loaded. Select [AE UMa](#result), choose L, and clear **Show references** and **Show check** for a single trace.
actions: Click one plotted dot, such as the point outlined in the screenshot. Each dot represents AE UMa in one exposure.
Read the selected filename in the frame selector. Open **Measurements** to inspect the matching row.
steps.check: The frame selector moves to the clicked observation. A trend extending over successive exposures can be compared with the reference stars; inspect a lone unusual point on its own image.
steps.alt: Measured AE UMa light curve with one actual observation outlined as the click target.

steps.title: Keep or change the comparisons
steps.requires: [Select AE UMa](#result) in Source Results and choose **L** in the Filter list.
actions: If the [reference and check traces](#references) look steady on the scale of the target’s variation, keep the automatic result and continue to the graph or report.
To see how a different group changes the same measurements, click **Scan Comps** above the plot.
steps.check: The comparison window opens for **AE UMa · [L]**. Its header gives the number of measured reference stars available to test.
steps.alt: AE UMa workspace with Scan Comps marked beside the filter and analysis controls.

links.label: Keep the automatic result and save the curve

steps.title: Build a pool of comparison candidates
steps.requires: The [Scan Comps](#scan-comps) window is on **1. Limits**.
actions: For this example, leave the brightness, color, and separation limits at **No limit**. Set **Comparisons per set (N)** to **3** (1). Each trial will then use three stars together.
Click **Build Candidates** (2).
steps.check: The window moves to **2. Favourites** and lists measured stars with their names, catalog brightness, and distance from AE UMa.
steps.alt: Search Limits panel for AE UMa showing three comparisons per set and the Build Candidates button.

steps.title: Choose which reference stars to test
steps.requires: You have [built candidates](#limits) and **2. Favourites** is visible.
actions: For this small example, click **Select All** (1). If you saw a blended or unstable reference on the images, clear its **Favourite** box. Keep at least three to build a set; four or more give you alternative three-star sets.
Click **Continue to Combinations** (2).
steps.check: The next page lists the possible three-star sets and calculates a preview for each.
steps.alt: Favourite Candidates table with its selection and Continue to Combinations buttons marked.

links.label: Change the pool size or limits

steps.title: Compare trial curves and apply a set
steps.requires: The [Favourites step](#favourites) has opened **3. Combinations**.
actions: Click a set in **Combination Sets** (1). Inspect the light curve, then click another set to see whether the pattern persists.
Use the preview list (2) to switch between **Filter [L]** and **Overview (with comps)**. Look for stable comparisons and a target trend that survives a change of reference stars.
Choose **Use Selected** (3) to apply the displayed set. Choose **Cancel** if you want to keep your previous result.
steps.check: Applying a set updates the AE UMa curve for the L filter. The Work Log identifies the comparisons used.
steps.alt: Comparison sets and a real preview curve, with the set row, preview mode, and Use Selected control marked.

links.label: Inspect the result in the workspace

groups.title: Save the graph or the measurements

steps.title: Save the light-curve graph
steps.requires: A [light curve](#axis) is visible. Select L and show the series you want in your saved figure.
actions: Click **Export** (1) above the plot.
For a clean figure, choose **Scientific** (2). For the graph as it looks in the workspace, choose **Theme-based** (3).
steps.check: The **Export light curve** file picker opens so you can choose where to save the figure.
steps.alt: Export menu above the AE UMa curve with Scientific and Theme-based marked as alternative choices.

steps.title: Name and save the plot file
steps.requires: Choose **Scientific** or **Theme-based** in the [plot Export menu](#plot-export).
actions: Navigate to a folder where you keep your results. With PNG selected as the file type, enter **AE-UMa-L.png** in the filename field (1).
Click **Save** (2). Open your saved image and check the star name, filter, and axes.
steps.check: A PNG file now contains the light-curve figure. Compare the shape with the exported example below.
steps.alt: Export light curve file dialog with AE-UMa-L.png entered and the Save button highlighted.

example.label: View the exported AE UMa light curve

steps.title: Export measurements for AE UMa
steps.requires: Click the [AE UMa row in Source Results](#result) first.
actions: Click **File** (1) in the menu bar.
Choose **Export Report** (2).
steps.check: The **AAVSO Preflight Review** opens. It checks which rows can go into the file format used by the American Association of Variable Star Observers and identifies missing information.
steps.alt: File menu displaying the Export Report action.

steps.title: Review the report before saving
steps.requires: You have opened [File → Export Report](#report-menu) for AE UMa.
actions: Read **Rows ready for AAVSO export**, **Skipped measurements**, and **Warnings**. Here 150 rows are ready for the export file and 8 were skipped. CAst lists an unmapped L filter, missing airmass, and a blank observer code. The **Standard rows** count alone cannot establish a Johnson V magnitude from these L frames.
Choose **Cancel** (1) if you need to correct the setup or revisit the reduction. To keep a local practice report after reading the warnings, click **Export Anyway** (2).

After export finishes, open the **science** folder beside the input images, then **AE_UMa**. Open **AE_UMa_measurements.csv** for the numbers. **AE_UMa_accepted_observations.csv**, **AE_UMa_rejected_observations.csv**, and **AE_UMa_aavso_preflight.json** document the export decisions.
steps.check: The Work Log records the export paths. Saving this bundle is a local operation. Review the warnings and scientific suitability separately before submitting any observation.
steps.alt: AAVSO Preflight Review from the actual AE UMa run with Cancel and Export Anyway marked.
